about.what: These two files (open-source-repository-sample.java-supplement.csv and this derivation) are a repository sample made by open-source-repository-sampler: a seeded, stratified sample of open-source repositories, each pinned to the commit that met the sampling criteria. This file records how the sample was derived and how to reproduce it.

command: open-source-repository-sampler sample --tiers high,mid,low --min-functions 50 --min-files-with-functions 15 --exclude-owners officefloor,sagenschneider --langs java --target 150 --label java-supplement --out-dir sample --seed 2
resolved_command: open-source-repository-sampler sample --langs java --tiers high,mid,low --target 150 --seed 2 --exclude-owners officefloor,sagenschneider --min-functions 50 --min-files-with-functions 15 --min-source-files 0 --min-nloc 0 --min-commits 0 --min-contributors 0 --min-language-share 0.0 --max-clones 2000 --pause 2.0 --out-dir sample --label java-supplement

because: no history criterion is set (min_commits, min_contributors are 0)

reproduce.the_same_code: open-source-repository-sampler checkout open-source-repository-sample.java-supplement.csv --dest repos  # every usable repository at its pinned commit
the_method: .venv/bin/open-source-repository-sampler sample --langs java --tiers high,mid,low --target 150 --seed 2 --exclude-owners officefloor,sagenschneider --min-functions 50 --min-files-with-functions 15 --min-source-files 0 --min-nloc 0 --min-commits 0 --min-contributors 0 --min-language-share 0.0 --max-clones 2000 --pause 2.0 --out-dir sample --label java-supplement
reproduce.note: Re-running the method draws afresh from GitHub as it is then: stars change and repositories come and go, so it reproduces HOW the sample was drawn, not necessarily the identical list. The CSV, with every repository pinned to a commit, is the record of WHAT was drawn.

method.frame: GitHub search/repositories per stratum (language x popularity tier), non-archived non-fork repositories, the excluded owners removed. Each tier is split into star bands (then creation-date bands) until every band matches at most 1000 repositories (GitHub's cap per query), and every band is fetched whole, so the frame is the complete population of the stratum as GitHub search lists it. A band that could not be split below the cap is marked truncated; see summary.truncated_bands. A failed search stops the run rather than leaving a gap.
method.draw_order: per stratum, the enumerated candidates sorted by name and shuffled by Python's random.Random seeded with '<seed>:<language>:<tier>': a simple random sample within the stratum, independent of every other stratum.
method.growth: in rounds, each language short of its target draws the next 1 candidate of each of its tiers in turn (tiers in the order given); a language stops the moment it has `target` usable repositories, or when its strata are exhausted.
method.allocation: disproportionate: tiers are drawn equally regardless of population, so the pooled sample over-represents high-star repositories, and the usable split across tiers follows each tier's exclusion rate. For estimates about the population, weight each stratum by population / usable from summary.per_stratum. Comparisons between tiers need no weights.
method.cross_stratum: a usable repository counts toward its detected language, not the GitHub label it was drawn under, so a repository mislabelled on GitHub enters with its label's stratum's sampling fraction; the CSV records both (language, stratum_language).
method.pin: each candidate is cloned at its default branch as it is when drawn; that commit is recorded and is what every measure and criterion describes. The clone is deleted once its row is written.
method.clone: shallow (depth 1): no history criterion is set, so the code at the pinned commit is all the criteria need; the history columns are left empty
method.language_detection: dominant language of the project's own source files (tests, vendored and generated code excluded; build-output directories excluded at the repository root only) by file count. `.h` headers are measured but do not vote (they are C or C++ by the other files; an all-header tree takes GitHub's label when it is C or C++, else C). A usable repository counts toward its detected language, not its stratum.
method.status: usable: measured and met every criterion; excluded: measured and did not (reason says which); error: could not be inspected (clone failed), kept apart because such loss can fall unevenly, e.g. on the largest projects when the full history is cloned.
method.usable_rule: measured; detected language in `langs`; and n_functions >= min_functions (functions parsed by lizard (tests excluded)); n_files_with_functions >= min_files_with_functions (source files holding a function); n_source_files >= min_source_files (source files of the project's own code); nloc >= min_nloc (non-comment lines of code); n_commits >= min_commits (commits reachable from the pinned commit); n_contributors >= min_contributors (distinct author emails in that history); language_share >= min_language_share (detected language's share of source files). Decided on these generic measures only, before any study looks at the repository. Function counts come from lizard and are not comparable across languages (it counts different constructs per language), so a fixed bound is a different threshold per language.
